title: Surviving a mistake at work
titleChinese: 如何妥善应对工作中的失误
paragraphs: That email you didn't send, the calculation you misread, the realisation that the deadline was yesterday... all followed by a sinking feeling, a quickening of the breath and the realisation that it's your fault. Fear not! Handled well, a mistake at work can become a great opportunity.

Start by owning up to it. It may be tempting to cover up a mistake, but any deception is unlikely to last for long and could delay attempts to put right the problem. And that's next – try to resolve the problems that you've created. Being proactive and coming to your manager with suggestions is likely to help you regain trust. Psychologists tell us that we tend to have a negativity bias – we are more likely to remember negative things. This is why executive coach Dina Denham Smith tells us we need to make our progress in fixing the issue clear and visible. It's also important to apologise. Showing genuine remorse demonstrates that we can take ownership of our blunders.

As well as looking at how we make amends for our mix-ups to other people, we also need to be honest with ourselves. Removing emotion is important. Shame from making a mistake can cloud our judgement when deciding how to respond. It can also affect our perception of the mistake's seriousness – it's easy to exaggerate how bad something really is. Everyone makes mistakes. What's really important is how we address them. It's important to be reflective. Consider if there's an underlying cause for the mistake, and how to prevent future slip-ups. It can also be useful to seek advice from someone who's had similar experiences in the past. Combined with our own reflections, this can be a powerful way to grow in our job and be more successful.

Academics Jasmine Virhia and Grace Lordan highlight research showing that workplaces which replace fear and blame around mistakes with opportunities for self-reflection are more psychologically safe. This allows people to learn from their mistakes, grow their skills, improve processes and ultimately productivity. Handled in the right way, by both employees and employers, mistakes can become a powerful tool for improvement.

vocabulary.entry: **calculation** /ˌkælkjuˈleɪʃn/ n. 计算
vocabulary.example: The calculation showed that the project would cost $1 million.
vocabulary.translation: 计算显示该项目将耗资100万美元。

vocabulary.entry: **misread** /ˌmɪsˈriːd/ v. 误读，读错
vocabulary.example: I misread the map and took the wrong turn.
vocabulary.translation: 我看错了地图，拐错了弯。

vocabulary.entry: **deadline** /ˈdedlaɪn/ n. 截止日期，最后期限
vocabulary.example: The deadline for applications is next Friday.
vocabulary.translation: 申请的截止日期是下周五。

vocabulary.entry: **sinking feeling** /ˈsɪŋkɪŋ ˈfiːlɪŋ/ n. 沮丧感，不祥的感觉（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: A sinking feeling came over me when I saw the exam paper.
vocabulary.translation: 看到试卷时，我心中涌起一阵沮丧。

vocabulary.entry: **own up to** /ˌəʊn ˈʌp tu/ phr. v. 承认（错误），坦白（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: He finally owned up to breaking the window.
vocabulary.translation: 他终于承认打破了窗户。

vocabulary.entry: **tempting** /ˈtemptɪŋ/ adj. 诱人的，有吸引力的
vocabulary.example: The offer of a free trip was very tempting.
vocabulary.translation: 免费旅行的提议非常诱人。

vocabulary.entry: **cover up** /ˌkʌvər ˈʌp/ phr. v. 掩盖，掩饰（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The company tried to cover up the scandal.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司试图掩盖丑闻。

vocabulary.entry: **deception** /dɪˈsepʃn/ n. 欺骗，欺诈（书面语）
vocabulary.example: He was found guilty of obtaining money by deception.
vocabulary.translation: 他被判犯有通过欺骗获取钱财的罪行。

vocabulary.entry: **put right** /ˌpʊt ˈraɪt/ phr. v. 纠正，改正（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The mechanic put right the problem with the engine.
vocabulary.translation: 机械师修好了发动机的问题。

vocabulary.entry: **resolve** /rɪˈzɒlv/ v. 解决（问题或困难）（书面语）
vocabulary.example: We need to resolve this issue as quickly as possible.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要尽快解决这个问题。

vocabulary.entry: **proactive** /prəʊˈæktɪv/ adj. 积极主动的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The proactive employee suggested a new marketing strategy.
vocabulary.translation: 这位积极主动的员工提出了新的营销策略。

vocabulary.entry: **regain** /rɪˈɡeɪn/ v. 重新获得，恢复（书面语）
vocabulary.example: She is trying to regain her confidence after the failure.
vocabulary.translation: 失败后她正努力重新找回自信。

vocabulary.entry: **negativity bias** /ˌneɡəˈtɪvəti ˈbaɪəs/ n. 消极偏见（心理学专业术语）
vocabulary.example: Negativity bias makes us focus more on bad news than good news.
vocabulary.translation: 消极偏见使我们更关注坏消息而非好消息。

vocabulary.entry: **executive coach** /ɪɡˈzekjətɪv kəʊtʃ/ n. 高管教练（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The executive coach helped the manager improve his leadership skills.
vocabulary.translation: 高管教练帮助这位经理提高了领导技能。

vocabulary.entry: **genuine** /ˈdʒenjuɪn/ adj. 真诚的，真正的
vocabulary.example: Her smile seemed genuine.
vocabulary.translation: 她的微笑看起来是真诚的。

vocabulary.entry: **remorse** /rɪˈmɔːs/ n. 悔恨，自责（书面语）
vocabulary.example: He showed no remorse for his actions.
vocabulary.translation: 他对自己的行为毫无悔意。

vocabulary.entry: **take ownership of** /teɪk ˈəʊnəʃɪp əv/ phr. 承担……的责任（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: You need to take ownership of your mistakes.
vocabulary.translation: 你需要为自己的错误承担责任。

vocabulary.entry: **blunder** /ˈblʌndə(r)/ n. 愚蠢的错误，疏忽（书面语）
vocabulary.example: His blunder cost the company a lot of money.
vocabulary.translation: 他的疏忽让公司损失了很多钱。

vocabulary.entry: **make amends for** /ˌmeɪk əˈmendz fɔː(r)/ phr. 弥补，补偿（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: He tried to make amends for his rude behaviour.
vocabulary.translation: 他试图弥补自己粗鲁的行为。

vocabulary.entry: **mix-up** /ˈmɪks ʌp/ n. 混淆，差错（口语）
vocabulary.example: There was a mix-up with the hotel reservations.
vocabulary.translation: 酒店预订出了差错。

vocabulary.entry: **cloud** /klaʊd/ v. 使模糊，使难以理解（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Anger clouded his judgment.
vocabulary.translation: 愤怒影响了他的判断。

vocabulary.entry: **exaggerate** /ɪɡˈzædʒəreɪt/ v. 夸张，夸大（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The media exaggerated the seriousness of the incident.
vocabulary.translation: 媒体夸大了事件的严重性。

vocabulary.entry: **address** /əˈdres/ v. 处理，应对（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The government must address the issue of climate change.
vocabulary.translation: 政府必须应对气候变化问题。

vocabulary.entry: **reflective** /rɪˈflektɪv/ adj. 反思的，沉思的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: She was in a reflective mood after the meeting.
vocabulary.translation: 会议后她处于反思的状态。

vocabulary.entry: **underlying** /ˌʌndəˈlaɪɪŋ/ adj. 潜在的，根本的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The underlying cause of the problem is poor communication.
vocabulary.translation: 问题的根本原因是沟通不畅。

vocabulary.entry: **slip-up** /ˈslɪp ʌp/ n. 疏忽，失误（口语）
vocabulary.example: A small slip-up in the calculations caused a big delay.
vocabulary.translation: 计算中的一个小疏忽造成了很大的延误。

vocabulary.entry: **psychologically safe** /ˌsaɪkəˈlɒdʒɪkli seɪf/ adj. 心理安全的（专业术语）
vocabulary.example: A psychologically safe workplace encourages open communication.
vocabulary.translation: 心理安全的工作场所鼓励开放沟通。

vocabulary.entry: **productivity** /ˌprɒdʌkˈtɪvəti/ n. 生产力，效率（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The new software has led to a significant increase in productivity.
vocabulary.translation: 新软件带来了生产力的显著提高。

sentences.chinese: 心理学家告诉我们，我们往往有消极偏见——我们更容易记住消极的事情。

sentences.chinese: 表现出真诚的悔恨表明我们可以为自己的错误负责。

sentences.chinese: 除了考虑如何弥补我们对他人的影响之外，我们也需要对自己诚实。

sentences.english: Removing emotion is important.
sentences.chinese: 消除情绪很重要。

sentences.chinese: 因犯错而产生的羞耻感会在决定如何回应时影响我们的判断。

sentences.chinese: 它还会影响我们对错误严重性的认知——人们很容易夸大事情的糟糕程度。

sentences.chinese: 每个人都会犯错。

sentences.chinese: 真正重要的是我们如何应对错误。

sentences.chinese: 考虑错误是否有潜在的原因，以及如何防止将来出现失误。

sentences.chinese: 向有过类似经历的人寻求建议也可能很有用。

sentences.chinese: 加上我们自己的反思，这可以成为在工作中成长并取得更大成功的有效途径。

sentences.english: This allows people to learn from their mistakes, grow their skills, improve processes and ultimately productivity.
sentences.chinese: 这使人们能够从错误中学习，提升技能，改进流程，最终提高生产力。

sentences.english: Handled in the right way, by both employees and employers, mistakes can become a powerful tool for improvement.
sentences.chinese: 如果员工和雇主都处理得当，错误可以成为进步的有效工具。
